summary: Weyerhaeuser No. 2 (Clam Mountain) lookout, Lewis County WA: wooden live-in tower built 1940, abandoned in the 1950s. Two moved footings were seen in 2018 on permit land.

facts.design: Wooden tower with a live-in cab
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s and gone. In 2018 only two footings were seen; they had been moved a considerable distance to make room for logging equipment that used the site as a landing.

access.note: Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm permit required. A motorized permit reaches the site; Willhite on a non-motorized permit parked at the Sorenson Road gate.

corrections.why: Willhite spells the company name Weyerhaeuser in the permit line and the page title; the register and the record spell it without the second e
Same spelling issue as the name; Willhite uses Weyerhaeuser for the company

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says gone and the washingtonlookouts list says removed. Willhite's 2018 visit found two footings moved on the logging landing, so the lookout is gone but some footings remain.

notes_for_editor: Elevation 2,687 ft (819 m) matches the record. The 1940 build date and the 1950s abandonment agree across the register, washingtonlookouts (attributed to Kresek) and Willhite. Willhite is the only source for the 2018 footings, the 1941 USGS note and the access details, so present-day facts rest on one visit. No staffing source was found. A firelookout.com page for this site returned 404 and was not used. Access: Willhite says a permit is required; washingtonlookouts lists the site as Private. The two spelling corrections are for human review. No photo URLs were available, so none were added.
